title: Electrophysiological Recording of Electrically-Evoked Compound Action Potentials
author: James B Fallon
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfwyjpfw

steps.title: Test array impedance post‑surgery
steps.instruction: Immediately after implantation surgery or in awake, unrestrained animals, use a custom stimulation to test the electrical impedance of the electrode array and identify any open or short‑circuit wires.

steps.title: Measure each electrode impedance
steps.instruction: Using biphasic current pulses, measure the impedance of each electrode by passing pulses between the electrode of interest and all other implanted electrodes; deliver a 25 ms per phase pulse at 931 mA and record the peak voltage at the end of the first phase (Vtotal).

steps.title: Connect functional electrodes
steps.instruction: If all electrodes are functional, connect one pair of electrodes to the stimulator and another pair to the electrophysiological recording equipment.

steps.title: Configure bipolar stimulation for ECAPs
steps.instruction: Set up a bipolar stimulation and recording electrode configuration to generate electrically‑evoked compound action potentials (ECAPs).

steps.title: Acquire two averaged ECAP datasets
steps.instruction: Make two sets of evoked electrophysiological recordings, each averaged from a total of 50 stimulus‑response trials.

steps.title: Apply stimulus current series
steps.instruction: Deliver biphasic pulses (width = 200 ms, interphase gap = 50 ms) at a rate of 10 pulses per second, stepping the stimulus current from 0 mA to 2 mA in 0.1 mA increments while recording the responses.

steps.title: Sample and filter recordings
steps.instruction: Sample the recordings at 100 kHz, apply a high‑pass filter at 200 Hz, a low‑pass filter at 2000 Hz, and set the voltage gain to 10³.

steps.title: Determine neural response threshold
steps.instruction: Define the electrically‑evoked neural response threshold as the minimum stimulus intensity that produces a response amplitude of at least 0.1 mV.
